pr_title: Add utility for asserting listeners are completed
pr_body:
Closes #108123

Because we can only be sure that the listener was not called when it finally gets GC'd, it may not fail tests that cause the situation to arise, or even log during them, as the GC may happen some time after they're completed, or in a separate VM. This is somewhat mitigated by the fact that `LeakTracker` will include the test name in the `contextHint`.

Perhaps it would be handy to be able to also trigger these checks in `@AfterEach` (i.e. potentially before GC) so for in-process tests we could fail the test in which the assertion was violated? I have an idea of how this might work
pr_comments:
> Certainly not so easy to test so thoroughly, but then again such a simple change doesn't need such comprehensive testing either.
> 
> That said, the leak tracker itself doesn't have such good test coverage today. I'd rather we fixed that rather than introducing something that's effectively a different implementation of the same thing with better tests.

This is a good point, I updated the PR to use `LeakTracker` directly. It actually helps with associating a leak with the test that caused it, because the test infrastructure already adds the test name in `LeakTracker#contextHint`.

~I didn't really beef up the testing of `LeakTracker` at all~, but added `ESTestCase#assertLeakDetected` which allows a test to assert that a leak was detected, and prevent failing because of it. That might be useful for writing more comprehensive `LeakTracker` tests? Happy to go ahead and do that if we think it's a good approach?

> Looks good, left some more comments. I suggest breaking out the leak-tracker tests into a separate PR too.

Comments are addressed now, I've applied the suggested changes and stored the LeakTracker locally ready to open a separate PR after this is merged (it depends on `assertLeakDetected`.

issue_context.title: Add utility for asserting listeners are completed
issue_context.body:
We have the `ActionListener#assertOnce` utility which actually asserts that the listener is called _at most_ once. We could make a similar utility to assert that a listener is called _at least_ once using `java.lang.ref.Cleaner`. Then we could combine them together into a utility that asserts that listeners are called _exactly_ once.

I expect there are some listeners for which such an assertion does not hold today because e.g. the completion is dispatched to a `GENERIC` thread which just quietly drops work on shutdown, the justification being that if the node is shutting down then it doesn't matter if we leak stuff locally, and remote listeners will be completed when the network connections close. IMO this is something of a bug, making it harder to reason about the behaviour during a truly graceful shutdown, although it's not super-important outside of tests indeed.

review_comments: This and the next one test the `ActionListenerImplementations.AssertAtLeastOnceActionListener` directly, as it was easier to do by providing a specific `NotCalledListener`. Using `MockLog#assertAllExpectationsMatched` seemed like a brittle way of testing that a log message _didn't_ appear.
